title: Same song twice
scenario: Did any song play twice in the set list?

intro.job: Did any song play twice in the set list?

idea.rule: Check every song against ALL the songs before it, not just the one next door.
idea.detail: A set remembers everyone you've seen so far, and 'song in seen' asks it in one step. Walk the list once: if the song is already in the set, that's a repeat; otherwise add it. A repeat can be anywhere earlier — not just right next door.

watch.code:
dup = False
seen = set()
for song in songs:
    if song in seen:
        dup = True
    seen.add(song)
print(dup)

model_restatement: Say True if any song appears more than once, otherwise False.

clarify.question: Could the same song be spelled differently?
clarify.answer: No — songs are clean and lowercase today.

clarify.question: Do you want which song played twice?
What if the list is empty or has one song?
clarify.answer: Then no song played twice — False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Go down the set list comparing each song with the next one. If they match, a song played twice. Print the answer.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 3 is the last comparison. What is i?
With the fix — iteration 4 (the second rock): after line 5, what is dup?

why_line: Comparing only neighbours checks rock–pop, pop–jazz, jazz–rock. The two rocks are three seats apart, so no neighbour pair ever matches.

explain.rule: Checking only the next seat is a bouncer who remembers one face — the second rock walks in three songs later and he's forgotten her.
explain.bridge: So what could remember EVERY song you've seen so far?

fix.rule: A set remembers every song so far; 'song in seen' checks all of them at once.

walk.gloss: Have we heard this song anywhere before?

fix.recommended:
dup = False
seen = set()
for song in songs:
    if song in seen:
        dup = True
    seen.add(song)
print(dup)

alternatives.note: A set drops repeats, so it's shorter if there was one — the shortcut.

hints: Which pairs does the draft actually compare?
The two rocks aren't next to each other.
Keep a set of songs heard so far and check 'song in seen'.

one_liner: Check every song against ALL the songs before it, not just the one next door.
